transcript.text: theres a funny smell from my oven when its on

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Please stop using the oven immediately and isolate it from the mains (switch off at the wall or fuse box). A 'funny' or burning smell when an oven is on can sometimes be normal dust burning off after a long period of non-use, but it is also a common sign of a loose or overheating electrical connection at the back of the appliance. This is a safety hazard and should not be ignored. To help me guide you further while you wait for an engineer: does the smell seem to come from inside the oven (like burnt food) or from the rear/back near where it meets the wall? And is it a plastic/rubber burning smell, or just a dusty 'hot' smell?
more like hot plastic or electrical, and it seems to come from behind or below, not inside the oven. its been like that 3-4 days and getting stronger

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Because the hot plastic/electrical smell is coming from behind or below the oven and has been getting stronger over several days, this points to a serious issue with the controls or wiring at the back of the appliance. This is likely caused by a failed cooling fan (which cools the control panel) or an overheating electrical connection. As I mentioned earlier, please do not use the oven again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. You should arrange for a professional to inspect it as soon as possible.
